rv.q: This is a sweet story, almost a fantasy, in some ways... In Simon Stephens' tightly constructed one-act, it actually works.

It’s pure fantasy, as is the idea that young lovelies pursue aging, socially awkward men, rather than the other way around. But this is the universe of “Heisenberg”: a place of feel-good plot devices pretentiously packaged as cosmic truths.
I finally concluded that I was working much too hard to make sense of a script that needs a complete rewrite with a clearer focus.

cn.t: Simon Stephens' two-hander receives a mixed response, with critics divided on whether strong performances can overcome a chaotic, uneven script that some find captivating while others deem confused and overly hysterical.
